Bennett University
Mr. Vineet Jain, a visionary leader and a media industry powerhouse, has significantly impacted
India's media and education landscape through his dedication to empowering youth. Inspired by
his belief in the potential of educated and engaged young minds, he founded Bennett University
in 2016, embodying his commitment to excellence and innovation in higher education.
As the Managing Director of India's oldest, largest, and most respected media conglomerate,
Bennett, Coleman & Co. Limited (known as The Times Group), Mr. Vineet Jain has played an
instrumental role in steering the entire spectrum of BCCL's operations. This includes overseeing
content creation and editorial strategies for the group even as he has driven the diversification
and expansion of what began as a traditional publishing business under the flagship The Times
of India into a diversified and expansive media empire.

With a peerless legacy of over 186 years, the Times Group has been a pillar of trust, knowledge, and public
service. Founded in 2016, Bennett University continues this proud tradition, shaping future leaders committed
to excellence, integrity, and global impact.
Accredited with an A+ grade by NAAC and recognised by the University Grants Commission (UGC),
Association of Indian Universities (AIU), and the Bar Council of India (BCI), Bennett University upholds the
highest educational standards. Its interdisciplinary curriculum fosters critical thinking, adaptability, and lifelong
learning, empowering students to address global challenges.
A true beacon of academic excellence, Bennett University stands dedicated to creating responsible global
citizens and thought leaders.

Innovation & Entrepreneurship
Bennett Hatchery Foundation, a registered Section 8 company, is the startup incubation arm of the Centre for
Innovation & Entrepreneurship (CIE) at Bennett University, empowering innovators to transform ideas into
scalable ventures. Recognised by Startup India, MSME, and the UP StartinUP Policy, the Hatchery supports
early-stage startups across ideation, validation, prototyping, and market growth. Open to students, faculty, staff,
and external entrepreneurs, it offers structured mentorship, access to world-class infrastructure, industry
partnerships, and funding support. With ₹5.5 crore secured through government-backed seed funding
programmes, Bennett Hatchery Foundation actively nurtures high-potential startups and strengthens the
university’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. CIE advances innovation at Bennett University through three integrated
verticals—Academics, Bennett Hatchery Foundation, and SPARK, the student entrepreneurship cell—creating
a vibrant, end-to-end startup ecosystem on campus.

Bennett University is committed to fostering collaborative partnerships with industry leaders to provide students with
practical training and research opportunities, bridging the gap between academia and industry. These partnerships
involve joint research and development efforts in emerging technologies such as AI, Big Data, and Cloud Computing, as
well as providing students with training, internships, and certification programs through collaborative partnerships with
industry partners such as Apple, AWS, Cisco, Grant Thornton and Xebia among others. The University is also focused on
integrating industry-specific knowledge into the curriculum, fostering immersive learning experiences and establishing an
incubation center to support startups and existing companies. In addition, the campus adoption program aims to make
students corporate-ready, while the NASSCOM, FutureSkills PRIME platform provides opportunities for continuous
self-paced learning and skill development in emerging technologies.
Bennett University also emphasises collaboration with other academic institutions in fields of commerce, business,
economics, management and law.

School of Global Pathways
Pursuing higher education abroad is a remarkable opportunity that broadens horizons, fosters
personal growth, and opens doors to global career opportunities. However, this journey often
comes with challenges—complex application procedures, cultural adaptation concerns, and
uncertainty about employment opportunities.
Global Programs at Bennett University provide students a seamless solution to address these
concerns. The programs are designed to offer students unparalleled international exposure
while 	ensuring 	a 	smooth 	and 	cost-effective 	transition 	to 	our 	renowned 	partner
universities—Iowa State University and Kent State University, USA and the University of
Essex, the University of Reading and the University of Birmingham UK. Through our structured
credit transfer system, students gain access to world-class academic resources at an optimal
cost.
Beyond academic excellence, the program enhances career prospects by enabling students to
work in their destination countries, equipping them with valuable global experience.

CSET101 - Computational Thinking and Programming
Course Type - Core L-T-P Format 2-1-4 Credits - 5
COURSE SUMMARY
This course aims to enable students to solve given problem in Python by using standard programming constructs. It helps students to build programs using the features
of object-oriented programming languages. This course provides learning to make use of Python inbuilt API’s.
COURSE-SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (CO)
CO1: Solve given problem in Python by using standard programming constructs.
CO2: Build programs using the features of object-oriented programming languages.
CO3: Make use of Python inbuilt APIs to write functions.
Detailed Syllabus
Module 1 (Contact hours: 8)
Why Python, Applications of Python, Versions of Python, Number system, Binary, Octal, Literals, Variables, Data types, Operators, Control Structures if/else/elif,
Nested if/else, Lists/Nested Lists, Tuple.
Module 2 (Contact hours: 10)
Iterative Control, While loop, For loop, Range, Break, Continue, Pass, Nested Loops, Loop inside if, List Operations, List comprehension, Membership operator,

Module 2 (Contact hours: 10)
Iterative Control, While loop, For loop, Range, Break, Continue, Pass, Nested Loops, Loop inside if, List Operations, List comprehension, Membership operator,
Functions, Default argument, required arguments, keyword argument, variable arguments, Function invoking, Nested functions, Lambda functions, Map Reduce,
Recursive Functions, Factorial, GCD using Euclid Algorithm, Dictionary Operations, Sets, Enumerators.
Module 3 (Contact hours: 10)
String Operations, Slicing, File Handling, Exception Handling, Modules, Namespaces, Local, Global, and Built-in Namespaces, Object Oriented Programming, Classes
and Objects, Encapsulation, Data abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Interactive Graphics, Displaying Images, Generating Colors, Graphics Objects, Entry
Objects, Turtle, Tkinter, Working with Widgets, Controlling Layout with Geometry Managers, Events and Event Handlers, Developing Interactive applications.

The lab component of this course is designed to practice computational problems to enable the students to develop computational thinking.

This course aims at teaching students to increase awareness regarding one’s role in improving one’s quality of life. They will be able to appreciate knowledge about

CO3: Reflect on the aspects of leadership, motivation and stress management.
CO4: Appreciate the nature of positive and proactive thinking and assertiveness.
CO5: Apply concepts, tools and frameworks of emotional intelligence and stress management.

CSET108 - Environment and Sustainability
Course Type - Core L-T-P Format 3-0-0 Credits - 3
COURSE SUMMARY
Environmental science is a practical and multi-disciplinary science that traverses the biophysical, geochemical, and social sciences and focuses on the interaction
between the living and non-living organisms, including the role of human impacts. Environmental studies focus on a wide range of environmental issues and their
solutions to emerging environmental problems that face current and future societies. These include climate change, biodiversity, water quality, natural resource
management, pollution, and environmental protection and conservation.
COURSE-SPECIFIC LEARNING OUTCOMES (CO)
CO1: Demonstrate analytical thinking skills concerning environmental topics .
CO2: Demonstrate an ability to combine the many disciplines and fields that intersect with environmental concerns.
CO3: Illustrate an integrative approach to environmental issues with a focus on sustainability.
Detailed Syllabus
Module 1 (Contact hours: 6)
Environmental sustainability, ecosystems and climate change: Introduction to environmental sustainability – Sustainability and population growth – growth curves –

Module 1 (Contact hours: 6)
Environmental sustainability, ecosystems and climate change: Introduction to environmental sustainability – Sustainability and population growth – growth curves –
Way forward – Ecosystems and climate change introduction – Ecosystem dynamics –Tragedy of commons - Tragedy of commons solutions – Ecosystems and
extinctions – Weather vs. Climate – Climate changes in the past – Climate change in the present – Climate processes.
Module 2 (Contact hours: 5)
Biodiversity and its conservation: Biodiversity – Value of biodiversity – Threats to biodiversity - Conservation of biodiversity – Case studies.
Module 3 (Contact hours: 8)
Natural resources: Natural resources - Associated problems with natural resources . renewable and non-renewable energy – Water and Agriculture - Agriculture and
Food – Problems and Solutions.
Module 4 (Contact hours: 8)
Environmental pollution: Causes, effects and control measures of various types of pollutions - Air pollution - Water pollution - Wastewater treatment - Soil pollution -
Noise pollution - Thermal pollution - - Solid waste management - E-waste - Case studies on pollution.
Module 5 (Contact hours: 7)

Noise pollution - Thermal pollution - - Solid waste management - E-waste - Case studies on pollution.
Module 5 (Contact hours: 7)
Environmental ethics and policies: Environment ethics – Global policies – Environmental laws in India – Environmental impact assessment - Issues involved in the
enforcement of environmental legislation.
Module 6 (Contact hours: 8)
Life cycle analysis and sustainability thinking: Introduction of LCA – Methodology of LCA – ISO 14044 Significance of LCA – Case studies of LCA .

e) Evaluation of Academic Performance
The performance of a student will be evaluated in terms of two indices, viz., the Grade
Point Average (SGPA) in a semester (which is the Grade Point Average for a semester) and
Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) which is the Grade Point Average for all the
completed semesters up to that point.

f) Grade Point Average (GPA)
The GPA is calculated based on grades obtained in all courses, except audit courses,

completed semesters up to that point.

f) Grade Point Average (GPA)
The GPA is calculated based on grades obtained in all courses, except audit courses,
registered for the semester and shall be reflected in the semester grade sheet. It is calculated
as below.

(a) Multiply the credits by the points assigned to the grade concerned.

(b) Add the total grade points for all the registered courses of the semester.

(c) Divide the total grade points by the total number of registered credits.

the period for which records are to be retained.
Purpose

duration of time.

(c) To ensure secure disposal of the same post that duration.
Scope

not limited to answer sheets, question papers, and attendance sheets) are preserved securely
during their life cycle and disposed of thereafter.

Policy
This policy outlines the process for retention and disposal of students’ answer sheets and
other examination-related records to be followed at Bennett University.
(a) Retention
The students’ answer sheets and related records are retained for a minimum period
of one academic year to address any examination-related grievances by the students

data stored safely in password-protected folders.

NOTIFICATION

The minimum attendance criteria for the students to appear in the End Semester
Examination was reviewed in the 13‘ Academic Council Meeting held on 29% July
2022 in consonance with the UGC’s (Minimum Standards of Instruction for the
Grant of the First Degree through Formal Education) Regulations, 2003.

The Competent Authority has approved that the students should have a minimum
attendance of 75% to become eligible for appearing in the End Semester
Examination with effect from the current semester onwards i.e. AY 2022-23 (odd
semester onwards). The Controller of Examination shall call for the attendance
record from the respective schools and check the eligibility keeping in view to the
minimum attendance criteria before allowing the candidature for appearing in the
examinations.

The respective schools shall maintain the attendance records subject wise and
shall be required to supply the information to the CoE for checking the eligibility
for examinations and to the O/o Registrar keeping in view, the requirement for the

shall be required to supply the information to the CoE for checking the eligibility
for examinations and to the O/o Registrar keeping in view, the requirement for the
Government Scholarship Cases and other verifying agencies.

The Deans of the respective Schools shall ensure that the faculty members mark
the attendance of the students on regular basis and the students/parents be
informed timely for any corrective actions with respect to shortage in attendance.

The IT Head shall ensure that the biometric attendance system is functional and
integrated with the CollPoll ERP, so that subject wise attendance of each student
is reflected on the Collpoll account of the students 4s well as the parents to avoid
any discrepancies.

7. GENERAL
1. No punishment shall ordinarily be imposed on a student unless he/she is found guilty of the

offence for which he/she has been charged by a proctorial or any other inquiry after following
the normal procedure and providing due opportunity to the student charged for the offence to
defend himself/herself.

In case the Vice Chancellor or any competent authority is of the opinion that on the basis of the
available material and evidence on record, a prima facie case exists against a student, s/he
may order suspension of the student including withdrawal of any or all facilities available a
to bona fide student pending proctorial or any other inquiry.
